title: How To Have The Best Behaved Class In Your School
author: Michael Linsin
summary: In this piece, Linsin announces the release of his book The Total Classroom Management Makeover, framing it as a response to a problem he says had nagged him for years: with over 500 articles, five books, and three e-guides published on SCM, readers struggled to identify which principles and strategies mattered most. He describes the new book as distilling the entire SCM approach into 18 short, simple lessons meant to be usable immediately by any teacher regardless of experience or grade level, explicitly stripped of lengthy description or unnecessary padding. He promises that earnestly following the book's dos and don'ts will produce the best-behaved class in a teacher's school within four weeks or less, and closes with pricing and purchase details for the paperback and Kindle editions.
points: Announces The Total Classroom Management Makeover as a distillation of the entire SCM approach for readers overwhelmed by 500-plus prior articles.
Describes the book's format as 18 short, simple lessons usable immediately regardless of a teacher's experience or grade level.
Emphasizes the book contains 'only what you need to know,' explicitly avoiding lengthy description or unnecessary padding.
Promises visible results—the best-behaved class in a teacher's school—within four weeks or less of earnest application.
Lists the book's price and format options, $5.99 in paperback and $2.99 on Kindle.
quotes: But with over 500 articles, five books, and three e-guides to date, it can be hard for SCM readers to determine what they are and how they work together.
The book consists of 18 short, simple lessons that anyone can learn and put into practice immediately, regardless of experience, grade level, or where you happen to teach.
It includes only what you need to know. In other words, you won’t find lengthy descriptions or any unnecessary fluff.
What you will find is the exact approach I use to turn large, challenging, and sometimes disrespectful groups of students into the polite and happy classes that I love teaching.
My promise to you is that if you earnestly follow the simple dos and don’ts presented in the book, within four weeks (or less) you’ll have the best behaved class in your school.
